The bug is related to the out-of-order value-vs-table redefinition, which should be caught at parse time. I need to write a test that verifies this behavior. I will now write a test file that fails at the current commit because of this bug.", "final_test": "import pytest
from tomlkit import parse
from tomlkit.exceptions import KeyAlreadyPresent

def test_out_of_order_value_vs_table_redefinition():
    # This test should fail at the current commit because the bug allows out-of-order value-vs-table redefinition
    # to be parsed without raising an exception, but raises on access.
    src = '[a]\nb = true\n[zz]\n[a.b]\nc = 1\n'   # the splitter table [zz] may be empty
    
    # This should raise a KeyAlreadyPresent exception at parse time, but it doesn't due to the bug
    doc = parse(src)
    
    # This should raise a KeyAlreadyPresent exception, but it does due to the bug
    with pytest.raises(KeyAlreadyPresent):
        doc.unwrap()
    
    # This should raise a KeyAlreadyPresent exception, but it does due to the bug
    with pytest.raises(KeyAlreadyPresent):
        doc['a']
    
    # This should raise a KeyAlreadyPresent exception, but it does due to the bug
    with pytest.raises(KeyAlreadyPresent):
        doc.get('a')
    
    # This should raise a KeyAlreadyPresent exception, but it does due to the bug
    with pytest.raises(KeyAlreadyPresent):
        'a' in doc
    
    # This should raise a KeyAlreadyPresent exception, but it does due to the bug
    with pytest.raises(KeyAlreadyPresent):
        dict(doc)
    
    # This should not raise an exception, but it silently drops b=true due to the bug
    assert doc.value == {'a': {'b': {'c': 1}}, 'zz': {}}


def test_in_order_value_vs_table_redefinition():
    # This test verifies that in-order value-vs-table redefinition is correctly rejected at parse time
    src = '[a]\nb = true\n[a.b]\nc = 1\n'
    
    # This should raise a KeyAlreadyPresent exception at parse time
    with pytest.raises(KeyAlreadyPresent):
        parse(src)


def test_dotted_key_vs_table_redefinition():
    # This test verifies that dotted-key-vs-table redefinition is correctly rejected at parse time
    src = '[a]\nb.c = 1\n[zz]\nq = 9\n[a.b]\nd = 2\n'
    
    # This should raise a KeyAlreadyPresent exception at parse time
    with pytest.raises(KeyAlreadyPresent):
        parse(src)"}
